zh.question: 火山为什么有的流出熔岩，有的喷出灰云？安静的火山以后还会喷吗？
zh.observe: 停在喷发时刻，依次选择熔岩流、喷泉和富灰爆发；保持方式不变再调供给。四个镜头保留同一时刻。推进到冷却看暗壳下的余热，再比较休眠与被认为熄灭的证据。

academic.title: 喷发方式与规模不能混成一个分数
academic.body: 岩浆上升时围压下降，溶解的挥发组分可以出溶形成气泡，气泡也会膨胀。流变和气体逸出影响熔岩溢流、喷泉或碎裂；温度、成分、晶体、供浆与外来水同样重要，低黏度并不保证没有爆炸。VEI 主要依据爆炸性喷出物体积，并结合喷发柱等证据，不等于全部能量或危险程度，也不是熔岩流量的刻度。本页供给滑块只控制示意的物质多少与范围。

academic.title: 材料的去向与山体的长期形状
academic.body: 火山灰是细碎岩石、矿物和火山玻璃，不是燃烧后的灰烬。较粗碎块可沿抛物线附近的轨迹落下，细灰受气流携带；真实输运还受粒径、风场、浮力和沉降影响。熔岩表面先冷却结壳，内部仍可保留大量热。多次熔岩与碎屑堆积塑造山体，盾状、成层火山和塌陷破火山口不对应一次喷发的弱、中、强；盾状火山也会有爆炸性喷发，破火山口也不一定靠猛烈爆炸形成。

academic.title: 休眠是间歇，熄灭是需要证据的判断
academic.body: 广义活火山包括当前喷发以及仍有潜力再次喷发的系统；休眠常指其中暂未喷发的时期。被认为熄灭，表示根据现有地质历史、构造和供浆背景，不再预期其喷发，并非对未来的绝对保证。各资料使用的术语和时间界线可能不同；不能仅凭安静多少年、植被或没有烟来判断。岩层年代、历史记录和地下活动线索须结合解释；一个旧喷口的活动终止，不排除火山区别处出现新喷口。

zh.misconception: “活火山”不等于一直喷，“休眠”不等于已熄灭；喷得亮、喷得高，也不是判断全部危险的尺子。
zh.boundary: 这是相对条件与证据的教学比较，时间、形状与尺度经过简化，不预测实际喷发、灰云或安全距离。

narration.label: 山下面有什么
narration.text: 看到火山喷出红亮的东西，你会不会以为山下面点着一堆火？其实那是很热的岩浆，里面有熔化的岩石成分，也可能有晶体和气体。它不是燃烧的木柴。我们从剖面开始，看看地下的岩浆，怎样沿着通道向上移动。
narration.cue: 停在地下剖面，指向通道。

narration.label: 气泡长大了
narration.text: 当岩浆来到更靠近地面的地方，周围压着它的力量常常变小，里面的一些气体就会形成气泡，气泡还会膨胀。有时气体比较容易出去，有时却没那么顺利。先慢慢推进，看看气泡和岩浆往哪里走，再猜猜改变条件会发生什么。
narration.cue: 推进减压与气泡阶段，留三秒预测。

narration.label: 同样喷发，不同模样
narration.text: 现在先把画面停住。点一下熔岩流，看红亮的岩石沿地面走；再点熔岩喷泉，看熔滴升起来，又落回去；最后看看灰云，它带着许多细细的岩石和玻璃碎片。这些可不是柴火烧完的灰！同一座火山也能换一种喷法。再调调供给，看看同一种喷法，是少一些，还是多一些。
narration.cue: 固定喷发进度依次切换三个示例；选择灰柱镜头，再单独改变供给。

narration.label: 安静的山，还有什么故事
narration.text: 这两幅安静的山，看起来一样呢！一座可能在两次喷发之间休息，我们常叫它休眠。另一座要研究很多证据，才可能被认为以后不再喷发。科学家会读岩石留下的记录，也观察地下的小地震和地面的变化。再看看旁边的山形，它们是很久很久积起来或塌下来的。海底也有火山，有些还能慢慢长出海面。我们去下一页找找，一座小岛是怎样来的吧。
narration.cue: 切换休眠与被认为已熄灭，强调山形相同而证据不同；观察三种地貌，接到海底火山专题。

en.question: Why do some eruptions make lava flows and others ash clouds? Can a quiet volcano erupt again?
en.observe: Pause during eruption and compare flows, fountains and ash. Keep the style fixed while changing supply. All four views preserve the same moment. Advance to cooling, then compare the evidence for dormancy and an extinction assessment.

academic.title: Style and size are different questions
academic.body: As magma rises, falling pressure allows dissolved volatiles to exsolve and gas bubbles to expand. Flow properties and gas escape influence effusion, fountains and fragmentation. Temperature, composition, crystals, magma supply and external water also matter; low viscosity does not rule out explosions. VEI primarily uses explosive ejecta volume together with plume evidence. It is not a score for total energy or hazard, nor a measure of lava discharge. Our supply slider changes only illustrative output and extent.

academic.title: Materials travel; volcano shapes accumulate
academic.body: Volcanic ash is fine rock, mineral and volcanic-glass fragments, not combustion ash. Coarser clasts may follow approximately ballistic paths; fine ash is carried by gas and air. Real transport depends on particle size, winds, buoyancy and settling. Lava surfaces form crust while interiors can retain substantial heat. Repeated lava and fragment deposits build landforms. Shield volcanoes, composite volcanoes and collapse calderas are not weak, medium and strong settings for one eruption. Shields can erupt explosively, and caldera collapse need not accompany a major explosion.

academic.title: Dormancy is an interval; extinction is an assessment
academic.body: Active in the broad sense includes systems erupting now and those still capable of eruption. Dormant commonly describes the latter between eruptions. An extinction assessment uses geological history, tectonic setting and magma supply, and can be revised. Definitions and time cutoffs vary; neither years of silence, vegetation nor absent emissions are decisive alone. Geological ages, records and subsurface clues require joint interpretation. An old vent becoming inactive does not exclude new activity elsewhere in its volcanic field.

en.misconception: Active does not mean always erupting, and dormant does not mean extinct. Glow and plume height are not complete measures of hazard.
en.boundary: This teaching comparison simplifies conditions, evidence, time, geometry and scale. It does not forecast eruptions, ash clouds or safe distances.

narration.label: What is under the mountain?
narration.text: A volcano may release glowing red material, but that does not mean someone lit a fire under the mountain. Very hot magma contains melted rock material and may contain crystals and gas. It is not burning wood. Begin with the cutaway and follow the route by which magma can move upward.
narration.cue: Hold the underground cutaway and point to the conduit.

narration.label: Bubbles grow
narration.text: As magma approaches the surface, the surrounding pressure often falls. Some of its dissolved gas can form bubbles, and those bubbles expand. Sometimes gas escapes readily; sometimes it cannot. Move forward slowly and watch where bubbles and magma go before predicting what a change in conditions might do.
narration.cue: Advance decompression and bubbles, then pause for three seconds.

narration.label: Different ways to erupt
narration.text: Pause the picture. Choose lava flows and follow the glowing rock along the ground. Choose fountains and watch lava clasts rise and fall. Then look at the ash cloud. It carries tiny rock and glass fragments, not ashes from a wood fire! The same volcano can erupt in different ways. Now change the supply and compare less or more material within one style.
narration.cue: Keep eruption progress fixed and switch the three examples; select the plume view, then change supply alone.

narration.label: A quiet mountain has a story
narration.text: These two quiet mountain pictures look the same! One volcano may be resting between eruptions: we call that dormant. Another may be considered unlikely to erupt again, after scientists study lots of evidence. They read rocks and observe small earthquakes and changes in the ground. Mountain shapes tell a much longer story of building and collapse. There are volcanoes under the sea too, and some can grow above the waves. Let us explore how an island can form.
narration.cue: Compare dormant and considered-extinct evidence while the mountain image stays the same. Observe the landforms and continue to submarine volcanoes.
